# Project rules

- Respond using direct voice.
- Component-test the in-progress state that names the step.
- Maintain a structured folder and code organization with clear module boundaries.
- Choose Auto or Selection mode up front and lock it when Style runs.
- Do not write DECISIONS.md as a spec dump, a work log, or a bullet list of what the code does.
- Use Vitest as the test runner for unit and integration tests.
- Unit-test that more than 2 characters and more than 1 chapter are refused.
- In each DECISIONS.md entry, state who proposed the decision (e.g., "my call" or "Claude proposed").
- After generating, only update or add project-specific changes on top of the generated files.
- Never re-send the full book text on later steps.
- Lint with npm run lint.
- Do not add shared constants, config, or indirection for values that are fixed requirements, such as the 2/1 image caps.
- In Selection mode, allow the text step to propose a larger candidate pool via CHARACTER_POOL or CHAPTER_POOL for the user to pick from.
- Upload the book once using the File API.
- Store the Gemini key in an environment variable.
- Perform all scaffolding work through the official generator.
- Split the frontend into focused component files.
- Do not add abstractions for features you are not shipping.
- Component-test the empty list state.
- Get explicit approval before deleting a branch, as with committing or pushing.
- Make the smallest change that fully does the task.
- During the Gradion assessment work, note and track the user's decisions as they are made throughout the conversation.
- Unit-test that a failed step is retryable while other steps are untouched.
- Never call Gemini from the client.
- Do not use Docker or a separate backend language or service; keep one Next.js app.
- Leave merged branches in place rather than removing them.
- Always wait for the user's approval before making any commit.
- Use page.tsx to compose components.
- Make every Gemini call server-side.
- For any env/config fix, update `.env.example` or describe the change in chat, and never touch the real `.env`.
- Run the official generator with the appropriate flags.
- Keep each DECISIONS.md entry concise.
- Get user approval for every commit, including documentation and code changes.
- Avoid dumping every option as a checklist.
- Use React Testing Library for component tests.
- Give each element Tailwind utility classes for styling.
- Cut preamble and do not restate what was already said.
- If the text yields no characters or chapters, fail the step with a delete-this-project or start-a-new-one message.
- Unit-test the backend step-order guard.
- Write in active/direct voice.
- Never make the semantic class name appearance-based.
- Write DECISIONS.md content as decisions in a discussion voice.
- Obtain approval before pushing to a remote, regardless of what changed.
- Never commit the Gemini key.
- Write concise and direct comments.
- Commit documentation and non-code changes on the current branch without creating a new branch.
- Write one or two paragraphs per decision covering who proposed it, the push-back, where it landed, and the trade-off.
- Write tests after the implementation for frontend states.
- Keep tests simple and targeted; do not over-test.
- Unit-test that a running step returns in-flight and is not duplicated.
- Write DECISIONS.md entries as a real decision/discussion between the user and the AI, not as a description of what the thing is.
- Once a decision is confirmed, record it as an entry in DECISIONS.md.
- Mock the Gemini SDK in all tests.
- Commit code changes only on a dedicated branch created for that work.
- Never edit the user's `.env` file.
- Obtain the user's explicit approval before making any commit, whether it contains docs or code.
- In written deliverables, keep entries modular and concise with a clear explanation rather than long over-written prose.
- Never delete a branch without an explicit user go.
- Never rely on the UI to enforce image caps.
- Never delete a branch on your own initiative.
- In each DECISIONS.md entry, include the trade-off.
- Check out a dedicated branch for a feature, fix, or next phase and commit there after approval.
- Do not narrate the obvious in comments.
- Use one consistent naming pattern across the codebase rather than ad-hoc names per function.
- Limit the project to at most 2 adult characters and 1 chapter, enforced server-side.
- Never record a decision mid-discussion or from your own proposal that the user has not accepted.
- Put code on its own branch.
- Keep implementation mechanics out of function names.
- Unit-test stuck recovery where a running and stale step becomes retryable.
- Run tests with npm test.
- Chain Gemini interactions by id using previous_interaction_id.
- Take a stance and argue for it briefly.
- Put reusable frontend components in src/components/.
- Remove dead code and needless work.
- Keep the files produced by the official generator.
- Lead a comment with the block's main purpose and mention how it runs only where non-obvious.
- Use a steady verb-plus-noun naming set.
- Put page-specific frontend components in a colocated _components/ folder.
- To tell the user what config or secret changes to make, edit `.env.example` with the right values and comments, or explain the change in chat.
- Never write or commit code directly on the main or master branch.
- Never let one file grow into a pile of components.
- Record a decision only after the user explicitly confirms it.
- State the point, then stop.
- Limit a finished project to at most 2 character portraits and 1 chapter illustration.
- Keep hot paths such as Gemini calls, polling, and file I/O lean.

- Do not replace generator-provided files such as configs, layout, page, or globals.css with hand-rolled versions.
- Invite the user to push back on your stance.
- In each DECISIONS.md entry, include the reason for the decision.
- Apply the same conciseness to written deliverables such as DECISIONS.md.
- Update DECISIONS.md, docs/plan.md, docs/tasks.md, and TESTING.md as part of the change, not as an afterthought.
- Write tests first for backend pipeline logic.
- When a real test run changes, refresh the TESTING.md count and report.
- Give each element a semantic class name for its meaning or role.
- Optimize for clarity first, then cost.
- Build with npm run build.
- Keep responses concise and direct.

- Never push without an explicit user go.

- Every decision entry should state why, not just what.
- Get approval before pushing to a remote, regardless of what changed.
- Reach for the smallest solution that fully does the task.
- Communicate configuration only via .env.example or chat.
- Well-known short forms such as id, db, err, prev, and tmp are allowed.
- Do not merely list options and wait for orders; participate in deciding.
- Put code on its own branch.
- Before writing a DECISIONS entry or committing, re-read the house rules.
- Produce TESTING.md describing what you test, what you skip, and why, plus a real test-run report.
- Write each DECISIONS.md entry concisely and in the user's first-person voice.
- Engage with the user as a peer rather than as a subordinate.
- Documentation and non-code changes may be committed on the current branch.
- Never work on code directly on main or master.
- Do not write E2E tests.
- Write each DECISIONS.md entry as a short narrative of the back-and-forth.
- Prefer right-sized solutions over clever ones.
- Put implementation mechanics such as locking and temp-file swapping inside the function and explain them with a short comment.
- Scaffold projects using official generators such as create-next-app instead of hand-writing the scaffolding.
- Use the official Gemini SDK rather than hand-rolled REST unless the SDK lacks an endpoint you need.
- Commit docs, decisions, planning, and other non-code changes on the current branch without checking out a new branch.
- You may delete merged branches only after the user asks.
- Stage and prepare changes, then wait for the user's go-ahead before committing.
- Use meaningful HTML elements such as header, nav, main, section, article, and button instead of div soup.
- Never retry a failed Gemini call in a loop.
- Keep responses short.
- When the user accepts your proposal, record your reasoning too.
- Add a length pre-check at project creation.
- Always capture the reasoning behind each decision, from both sides.
- Push back when you disagree rather than silently complying.
- Do not provide in-project recovery when the text lacks characters or chapters.
- Keep DECISIONS.md entries concise.
- Do not read or edit the user's .env file.
- Layer project-specific code and configuration on top of the generated output.
- Do not log trivia or non-project chatter.
- Start the app with npm run dev after running npm install.
- Keep the output produced by the official generator.
- On this project, act as a coworker/copilot who collaborates, not as an order-taker.
- Never commit without an explicit user go.
- Stage or prepare changes, then wait for the user's go before committing.
- In each DECISIONS.md entry, state what the user and AI agreed or did not agree on.
- In each DECISIONS.md entry, state what the user pushed back on.
- Never read, open, `cat`, or `sed` the user's `.env` file.
- Do not use cryptic single-letter names; use names such as user, project, chapter, and index.
- When the user pushes back or makes their own call, record the user's reasoning.
- Never delete git branches.
- Track only decisions related to the project, not every decision.
- Ship .env.example.
- Take clear positions on the work instead of staying neutral.
- Factor shared logic into reusable helpers instead of copy-pasting.
- Only retry a failed Gemini call when the user triggers the retry.
- Discuss trade-offs explicitly when working through decisions.
- Lock the JSON storage file and use atomic temp-write/rename when writing it.
- Component-test the error-with-retry state.
- Converge on a decision together with the user.
- Check out a branch for code changes and commit there only after receiving approval.
- Keep both the semantic class name and Tailwind utility classes on the same element.
